title: Dream Sweep Propels Liberty to First WNBA Finals Since 2013 – ESPN Exclusive
body:
The Atlanta Dream clinched a dramatic 85‑83 victory over the New York Liberty on Friday night, securing their first appearance in the WNBA Finals since the franchise’s inaugural postseason run in 2013. Angel Reese led the charge with 22 points, while Rhyne Howard contributed 21, and a late surge in the fourth quarter turned a tightly contested series into a decisive win for the Dream.

The Game 3 showdown was a roller‑coaster from tip‑off. New York jumped out to an early 12‑point lead, buoyed by a flurry of three‑pointers from veteran guard Sabrina Ionescu. Atlanta, however, responded with a balanced attack, leveraging the inside presence of Emma Meesseman and the perimeter shooting of Kysre Gibson. The teams exchanged leads throughout the first half, entering the locker rooms tied at 42‑42. The Dream’s resilience was evident in the second half, as they outscored the Liberty 23‑19 in the third period, largely thanks to Reese’s aggressive drives and Howard’s mid‑range accuracy.

The decisive moments arrived in the final five minutes. With the game knotted at 78‑78, the Dream executed a crucial defensive stop, forcing a turnover that set up a fast‑break dunk by Meesseman. Reese then sank two free throws to give Atlanta a two‑point edge. New York answered with a three‑pointer from Ionescu, but a missed foul on the subsequent possession allowed the Dream to regain possession. Howard’s clutch three‑point shot with 1:12 left on the clock stretched the lead to five, and the Liberty could not recover, missing a potential game‑tying three‑pointer in the final seconds.

Atlanta’s resurgence marks a significant turnaround for a franchise that has struggled to find consistency over the past decade. After a series of early‑round exits and roster overhauls, the Dream’s front office made decisive moves in the 2025 off‑season, acquiring Reese from the Chicago Sky and adding Howard in a high‑profile trade. Both players have integrated seamlessly, providing the scoring punch and defensive intensity the team lacked in previous campaigns. Coach Tanisha Wright’s emphasis on a “dual‑star” system—leveraging Reese’s athleticism alongside Howard’s versatility—has paid dividends, as evidenced by their combined 43 points in the clinching game.

The Liberty, meanwhile, face a sobering end to a season that began with high expectations. Led by Ionescu’s playmaking and a solid supporting cast, New York’s offense was potent but faltered in late‑game execution. The narrow loss underscores lingering issues with defensive communication and rebounding, areas the coaching staff will need to address in the upcoming draft and free‑agency period. Veteran guard Betnijah Laney, who posted 16 points and eight rebounds, expressed disappointment but remained optimistic about the team’s core returning for next season.

Looking ahead, the Dream’s berth sets up a compelling Finals matchup against the Western Conference champion Seattle Storm, a team that has dominated the league in recent years with its deep roster and seasoned leadership. Atlanta’s blend of youthful explosiveness and veteran poise will be tested against Seattle’s disciplined, defense‑first approach. If the Dream can sustain the momentum generated by Reese and Howard and tighten up their perimeter defense, they stand a realistic chance of ending a 13‑year championship drought. The stage is now set for a historic showdown that could reshape the balance of power in women’s professional basketball.
